questions.text: Tell me about a time you resolved a shipment delay that was impacting a key customer.

key_points: Root cause: carrier, customs, capacity, weather
Actions taken: rerouting, expediting, alternative carrier
Customer communication and relationship preserved
strong_answer_signals: Proactive customer contact before they escalate
avoid: Waited for delay to resolve itself

questions.text: Describe a time you reduced transportation costs without compromising service levels.

key_points: Analysed freight spend by lane, mode, carrier
Lever used: carrier consolidation, mode shift, load optimisation
Cost savings achieved and service level maintained

questions.text: Tell me about a time you improved warehouse throughput or efficiency.

key_points: Identified bottleneck (receiving, picking, packing, dispatch)
Change implemented: layout, process, technology
Throughput improvement measured

questions.text: Describe a time you managed a logistics crisis — e.g., port congestion, natural disaster, or carrier bankruptcy.

key_points: Immediate triage and impact assessment
Alternative routing or carrier secured
Business continuity maintained and lessons documented

questions.text: Tell me about a time you negotiated a carrier or 3PL contract that delivered significant value.

key_points: Preparation: market benchmarking, volume data, alternatives ready
Negotiation levers: volume commitment, payment terms, multi-year deal
Savings and service improvement secured

questions.text: What is the difference between FTL, LTL, and parcel shipping and when do you choose each?

key_points: FTL: full dedicated trailer, volume >12 pallets, time-sensitive
LTL: shared trailer, 1-12 pallets, cost-optimised
Parcel: small packages, last-mile, e-commerce
strong_answer_signals: Cost per unit weight by mode

questions.text: How do you calculate and monitor freight cost per unit shipped?

key_points: Total freight cost / total units shipped by lane
Normalise for weight and cube (cost per kg or CBM)
Trend monitoring and benchmark vs industry rate
avoid: Total cost only with no normalisation

questions.text: Explain incoterms and give examples of when you would use EXW, FOB, and DAP.

key_points: EXW: buyer takes all risk from factory gate (import experience needed)
FOB: risk transfers at origin port (common for ocean freight)
DAP: seller delivers to named place, buyer pays import duty

questions.text: What is a warehouse management system (WMS) and what core functions does it perform?

key_points: Receiving, put-away, picking, packing, dispatch, returns
Slot optimisation and wave planning
Integration with ERP and TMS
strong_answer_signals: Named systems used (SAP WM, Manhattan, HighJump)

questions.text: How do you design a network of distribution centres to minimise total logistics cost?

key_points: Demand mapping: where are customers and volumes
DC location modelling: transport cost vs facility cost trade-off
Service level constraints (next-day, 2-day) shape network

questions.text: A key carrier has suddenly increased rates by 30%. How do you respond?

key_points: Market benchmark: is this above market or inline?
Short-term: negotiate or activate secondary carrier
Long-term: diversify carrier base, RFQ process
avoid: Switch immediately with no due diligence

questions.text: Your warehouse is running out of storage capacity ahead of peak season. What do you do?

key_points: Immediate: racking optimisation, cube utilisation, slow-mover clearance
Short-term: overflow 3PL space or pop-up storage
Long-term: capacity planning review and lease/expand

questions.text: Customs holds your largest import shipment for inspection. It is due for a major product launch. What do you do?

key_points: Engage customs broker immediately for expedited clearance
Communicate risk to commercial and supply chain teams
Explore partial release or alternative stock options
strong_answer_signals: Broker engaged in hours not days

questions.text: You are asked to reduce your logistics team headcount by 20% while maintaining service levels. How do you approach this?

key_points: Process automation and technology first
Rebalance workload across remaining team
Retain critical knowledge; transparent communication
avoid: Across-the-board cut with no process change

questions.text: A customer claims their order arrived damaged. How do you handle the claim and prevent recurrence?

key_points: Immediate: acknowledge, investigate proof of delivery and photos
Resolution: replacement or credit based on policy
Root cause: packaging, carrier handling, loading

questions.text: What excites you most about working in logistics?

key_points: Real-world tangibility — physical goods movement
Complexity: global networks, real-time decisions
Impact: cost, service, customer experience

questions.text: How do you keep up with changes in freight markets and logistics technology?

key_points: Industry publications (FreightWaves, JOC, Logistics Management)
Carrier and 3PL relationship intelligence
Technology scouting: TMS, visibility platforms, automation

questions.text: Where do you see logistics technology heading in the next five years?

key_points: Real-time visibility and supply chain control towers
Automation: autonomous vehicles, warehouse robotics
AI for demand-sensing and dynamic routing

questions.text: How do you build and maintain strong 3PL and carrier relationships?

key_points: Regular QBRs with KPI review and improvement plans
Strategic partnership not just transactional
Volume transparency and growth plans shared

questions.text: How do you build a high-performing logistics operations team?

key_points: Hire for operational mindset and resilience
Clear KPIs, daily huddles, visual management
Development path and cross-training
avoid: No performance metrics for the team

questions.text: How do you measure and improve on-time delivery (OTD) performance?

key_points: Definition: promised vs delivered date at line level
Root cause analysis by lane, carrier, origin
Corrective action: carrier change, lead time buffer, process fix
avoid: No root cause or corrective action

questions.text: Tell me about a time you introduced a new technology or system into a logistics operation.

key_points: Business case and need identified
Change management: training, pilot, rollout
Adoption rate and operational improvement

questions.text: Describe a time you improved last-mile delivery performance for end customers.

key_points: Identified failure point: carrier, address quality, slot management
Intervention: carrier change, delivery window management, customer comms
CSAT or delivery success rate improvement
avoid: Addressed logistics KPI but not customer experience

questions.text: You discover your 3PL is systematically overbilling you. How do you handle it?

key_points: Audit and quantify the discrepancy with evidence
Formal dispute raised with contract reference
Credit recovery and audit clause added going forward
avoid: No contract or process change to prevent recurrence

questions.text: What is cross-docking and when is it used?

key_points: Direct transfer from inbound to outbound with minimal storage
Use cases: fresh food, retail flow, hub consolidation
Requirements: synchronised inbound and outbound, WMS/TMS integration
avoid: No practical use-case or constraint discussion

questions.text: Tell me about a time you improved visibility across your logistics network.

key_points: Gap: what could not be seen and why it mattered
Solution: visibility platform, carrier API, manual tracking replacement
Operational improvement from better visibility

questions.text: How do you balance cost optimisation and sustainability in logistics?

key_points: Mode shift: rail and ocean over air where possible
Load optimisation reduces fuel per unit
Carbon accounting and carrier sustainability scoring

questions.text: How do you manage logistics cost during periods of high freight market volatility?

key_points: Hedging: long-term contracts for base volume
Spot market only for overflow; monitor weekly
Demand planning accuracy to reduce spot exposure
